title: Exact dynamics of first-order system-bath coherence in bilinear bosonic models
authors: Yang-Yang Xie, Song-Lin Wu, Paul Brumer, Zhao-Ming Wang, Lian-Ao Wu
abstract: We investigate the exact dynamics of first-order system--bath coherence induced by excitation exchange in bilinear bosonic models. By solving the linear Heisenberg equations, we obtain the exact evolution of system and bath operators and evaluate the first-order coherence between the system mode and the collective bath mode directly coupled to it. We analyze how this coherence depends on initial occupations, coupling strength, spectral width, and detuning, showing that its buildup and oscillatory behavior are closely related to excitation exchange and reservoir memory. We further examine controlled coherence dynamics under leakage-elimination-operator inspired modulation of the system frequency. The results show that random modulation can suppress excitation leakage and maintain finite and relatively stable coherence fluctuations at long times. These results clarify the evolution and control of first-order system--bath coherence in settings where a localized bosonic mode is coupled to a structured bosonic reservoir.
summary: The paper theoretically analyzes how first-order coherence builds and evolves when a single bosonic mode interacts with a structured bath. By solving the full linear equations of motion, the authors demonstrate that reservoir memory effects (narrow spectral width) enhance transient coherence peaks. Furthermore, they show that active control via random frequency modulation can effectively suppress energy leakage into the environment, stabilizing quantum coherence at long times.
main_problem: The study investigates the exact dynamics of first-order system–bath coherence induced by excitation exchange in bilinear bosonic models.
main_result: Random frequency modulation is shown to be superior to periodic modulation for suppressing excitation leakage and maintaining stable, finite long-time coherence fluctuations.
method: The authors solve the linear Heisenberg equations exactly, avoiding approximations like Born or Markov limits, to derive time evolution coefficients for system and bath operators.
model_or_system: The model uses bilinear bosonic Hamiltonians describing a localized bosonic mode coupled to a structured continuum reservoir (e.g., cavity coupled to photonic/phononic crystal modes).
key_observables: First-order system–bath coherence ($C(t)$), system occupation number ($n_s(t)$), and the time evolution of coupling coefficients.
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($\Gamma$), spectral width ($\gamma$, controlling bath memory time), detuning ($\Delta = \Omega - \omega_0$), and modulation parameters ($\delta\omega_{	ext{max}}$, $	au_{	ext{ran}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the linearity of the Heisenberg equations, allowing for closed-form solutions for expansion coefficients.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the effect of system temperature ($T_s$), spectral width ($\gamma$), and detuning ($\Delta$) on coherence. Crucially, they compare random versus rectangular modulation protocols, demonstrating random modulation's superior ability to suppress leakage and maintain coherence.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving exact dynamics using linear equations, analyzing the dependence of coherence on reservoir spectral features (memory/detuning), and finally developing a control scheme using LEO-inspired frequency modulation techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous analytical insights into non-Markovian open quantum system dynamics, which is crucial for designing robust quantum devices where environmental coupling must be precisely controlled to preserve coherence.
